comments.content: The launch command was changed from `create_subprocess_shell` with a list to `create_subprocess_exec`. Previously the list was passed as a single argument to the shell (which is a bug, but the shell would still parse it). Now with `create_subprocess_exec`, the first positional argument is `self.config.browser_binary_path`, which may be `None` when the user has not provided a custom binary path. In that case `create_subprocess_exec(None, ...)` will raise a `TypeError`. The previous code path relied on `CHROME_ARGS` containing the binary? Actually no — the old code also passed `self.config.browser_binary_path` as the first element of the list. But the old code used `create_subprocess_shell` with `shell=False`, which is itself broken. Either way, this branch is only reached when `browser_binary_path` is set (the `_setup_user_provided_browser` path), so please confirm. If `browser_binary_path` can be `None` here, this will crash.

`chrome_remote_debugging_port` defaults to `CHROME_DEBUG_PORT` (9222). However, the docstring says it is used 'when browser_binary_path is supplied'. Since the default is non-None, the `--remote-debugging-port` arg is now always injected via `CHROME_DEBUGGING_ARG`, which is fine, but the field being `int | None` with a non-None default means users cannot easily disable it. Consider whether `None` should be allowed to skip the arg entirely, or document that it must be an int.

If `self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port` is `None`, `s.connect_ex(('localhost', None))` will raise a `TypeError`. Also, `chrome_args.remove(f'--remote-debugging-port={self.config.chrome_remote_debugging_port}')` would try to remove `'--remote-debugging-port=None'` which won't be present (since `CHROME_DEBUGGING_ARG % {...}` would produce `'--remote-debugging-port=None'` — actually it would, so remove would succeed but the arg is invalid). Guard against `None` here.

The set literal `{...}` is used to deduplicate args, but sets are unordered. The comment acknowledges this ('usually preserves the order, but not guaranteed'). For Chrome CLI args, order can matter (e.g., `--user-data-dir` before other flags). Consider using `dict.fromkeys(...)` to preserve insertion order while deduplicating.
